region_name: South & Southeast: Quinault, Enchanted Valley, LaCrosse, Duckabush, Staircase
summary: The wet, wild south side of Olympic National Park: the East Fork Quinault rain forest to Enchanted Valley's waterfall walls and historic chalet, up to Anderson Pass; the high O'Neil Pass traverse to Marmot, Hart and LaCrosse lakes and down the long Duckabush; the North Fork Quinault to Low Divide with the expert Skyline ridge; and the drier North Fork Skokomish from Staircase over First Divide with Flapjack Lakes and Six Ridge. As of early October 2026 the Quinault side is open (Graves Creek and the North Fork reached only via North Shore Road; the East Fork/Enchanted Valley is a trial quota area) while nearly every Staircase wilderness trail and camp remains closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire. Bear canisters are mandatory everywhere, and unbridged fords (White Creek, Upper Duckabush, Sixteen Mile, Wild Rose, Big Creek, Nine Stream) are the signature hazards.

nodes.name: Graves Creek Trailhead
nodes.description: The gravel road gives out in a clearing ringed by giant firs, and the first thing you hear is Graves Creek hurrying under its high bridge. Everything smells of wet bark and moss; the rain forest begins right at the bumper.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: parked car with an open trunk and a wooden trailhead sign with a map board; midground: a high log-and-plank bridge over a white-water creek; sky: a narrow grey band dithered blue/grey between tall dark-green conifers; landmark: an enormous Douglas-fir trunk framing the left edge. Colors: dark green, brown, grey, cyan water.

nodes.name: Graves Creek Campground

camp.reservation_or_quota: Front-country campground; NPS lists about 30 sites (first-come basis assumed; verify).
camp.water: Graves Creek / Quinault River nearby; potable water not verified
camp.notes: Road-end campground beside the trailhead; RVs and trailers prohibited on Graves Creek Road.

nodes.description: A handful of mossy sites under dripping maples at the very end of the valley road. Fall asleep to the river and you are already on the trail tomorrow.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small dome tent and a picnic table furred with moss; midground: bigleaf maples draped in green; sky: twilight dithered dark blue/black through branches; landmark: a campfire ring glowing light red.

nodes.name: Graves Creek Primitive Trail junction
nodes.description: Just past the bridge a faint path peels off south toward Success Creek and Lake Sundown, while the broad old road grade of the East Fork trail rolls on ahead.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a weathered wooden signpost with two arrows; midground: a wide, fern-edged old road grade and a skinny path vanishing into salal; sky: barely visible through canopy; landmark: a nurse log sprouting a row of seedlings.

nodes.name: Pony Bridge

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area: East Fork Quinault/Enchanted Valley trial quota (begun 2024, up to 3 years) of max 208 users or 30 permits per night; no itinerary deviation except emergencies.
camp.water: East Fork Quinault River below the bridge (treat).
camp.notes: Three small sites just north of the bridge. Rec.gov lists it 2.5 mi from the trailhead. Trail bridge was replaced in 2023.

nodes.description: The trail drops steeply and suddenly you are standing on a bridge over a slot of green water, its rock walls hung with maidenhair ferns. The river roars below like a long-held breath let out.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a timber bridge railing in brown; midground: a narrow gorge with emerald-cyan water churning white; sky: none, only overhanging fir boughs; landmark: dripping fern-covered rock walls. Colors: cyan, light cyan, dark green, brown, white foam.

nodes.name: Fire Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area: East Fork Quinault/Enchanted Valley trial quota (begun 2024, up to 3 years) of max 208 users or 30 permits per night; no itinerary deviation except emergencies.
camp.water: Fire Creek and the East Fork Quinault (treat).
camp.notes: Forested sites where the trail crosses Fire Creek on a foot-log, about 3/4 mi past Pony Bridge per the NPS trail guide; the Recreation.gov listing calls it '4 miles from trailhead'.

nodes.description: A single log, flattened on top, carries you over Fire Creek into a flat where moss-coated maples lean over the river. It is a soft, quiet place to stop early.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a flattened foot-log with a hand line over a clear creek; midground: bigleaf maples bearded in moss; sky: pale grey dither through gaps; landmark: a mossy boulder shaped like a sleeping animal.

nodes.name: O'Neil Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area: East Fork Quinault/Enchanted Valley trial quota (begun 2024, up to 3 years) of max 208 users or 30 permits per night; no itinerary deviation except emergencies.
camp.water: East Fork Quinault River, about 100 ft below the trail (treat).
camp.notes: Signed side trail drops about 100 ft to six brushy riverside sites with a privy. Very popular midway stop; Rec.gov says 7 mi from the trailhead, WTA 6.7.

nodes.description: A side path tips down to the river, where tents tuck into the brush beside rolling gray-green water. Woodsmoke, rushing water, and the clink of somebody's pot lid.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent among salmonberry; midground: a cobble river bar and a wide braided river; sky: grey-blue dither with low cloud; landmark: a far forested ridge in dark green with a white thread of waterfall.

nodes.name: Pyrites Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area: East Fork Quinault/Enchanted Valley trial quota (begun 2024, up to 3 years) of max 208 users or 30 permits per night; no itinerary deviation except emergencies.
camp.water: Pyrites Creek and the East Fork Quinault (treat).
camp.notes: Six sites on each side of Pyrites Creek in a bigleaf maple grove (12 total). NPS lists pit toilets only at Pony Bridge, O'Neil Creek and Enchanted Valley. Rec.gov says 10 mi from trailhead; WTA puts the creek at 9.5 mi.

nodes.description: Old maples stand in a loose ring here, their limbs thick with moss and licorice fern, and a clear creek splits the camp in two. It feels like a living room the forest arranged on purpose.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a foot-log bridge over a cobbled creek; midground: a grove of wide-armed maples furred in light green; sky: soft grey through yellow-green leaves; landmark: a single tent glowing in late light.

nodes.name: East Fork Quinault high bridge
nodes.description: A gate, then a tall bridge strung about twenty feet above the river. In spring old snow can cling to its planks, and the water below is loud enough to feel in your ribs.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: bridge deck with a patch of white snow; midground: a deep channel of foaming cyan water; sky: first opening of sky in miles, light blue dither; landmark: the valley walls ahead streaked with white waterfall lines.

nodes.name: Enchanted Valley

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area: East Fork Quinault/Enchanted Valley trial quota (begun 2024, up to 3 years) of max 208 users or 30 permits per night; no itinerary deviation except emergencies.
camp.water: East Fork Quinault River and side streams (treat).
camp.notes: Large forested camp area near the chalet; two privies. Bear canisters mandatory here since 2015 and hanging food is prohibited. Fires only in existing rings and only when no fire ban is in place. Very busy on weekends and holidays. Stay 50+ yards from bears.

nodes.description: The forest opens into a long meadow beneath cliffs so tall the waterfalls seem to fall from the clouds. Elk graze near the river, a black bear ambles along the far edge, and a log chalet waits in the grass like the cover of an old storybook.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tall meadow grass with a black bear at a distance; midground: the two-and-a-half-story log chalet with steep roof; sky: light blue with white cloud wisps dithered against grey cliffs; landmark: sheer dark-grey walls streaked with many thin white waterfalls. Colors: light green, dark grey, white, brown, light blue.

nodes.name: Enchanted Valley Chalet
nodes.description: Built of hand-hewn logs around 1930-31, the chalet once sheltered horse-packers and wartime aircraft spotters. In 2014 it was jacked onto steel beams and pushed about 100 feet back from the eroding river; it still waits there, closed, while the river keeps nibbling.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a cut riverbank with exposed roots and gravel; midground: the log chalet resting on cribbing and steel beams, windows shuttered; sky: misty grey-white dither; landmark: waterfall-streaked cliff behind the roofline.

nodes.name: White Creek ford
nodes.description: White Creek tumbles down from the high basins in a fan of cold, milky water. There is no bridge: in late summer it is a rock-hop, after rain or snowmelt it is a shin-numbing wade.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wet cobbles and a pair of trekking poles planted in current; midground: a wide, fast, pale-cyan creek with white riffles; sky: grey dithered cloud; landmark: steep green slopes with snow patches above.

nodes.name: O'Neil Pass Trail junction (East Fork)
nodes.description: A sign points south onto a thinner trail that climbs toward O'Neil Pass; the main path keeps switchbacking up toward Anderson Pass. Wind starts to come down the valley here, cool and smelling of snow.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a lone signpost with carved letters; midground: a rocky creekbed draining White Mountain; sky: light blue with a hard white cloud edge; landmark: rugged grey peaks with snowfields.

nodes.name: Anderson Pass
nodes.description: A narrow forested notch at the head of the valley, where the trail tips over toward the Dosewallips. Glacier-carved peaks crowd close; a side trail climbs toward the moraine and what is left of the Anderson Glacier.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail summit marker and a pack resting against a subalpine fir; midground: heather and snow patches; sky: deep blue dithered to light blue; landmark: Mount Anderson's dark rock and a shrinking white glacier.

nodes.name: O'Neil Pass
nodes.description: After miles of contouring through meadow and rock, the trail tops out on a grassy saddle. The Duckabush valley falls away at your boots, and the peaks of the southern Olympics line up like a row of storybook castles.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a hiker silhouette and a cairn; midground: alpine meadow with lupine purple and paintbrush red; sky: gradient dithered deep blue to cyan; landmark: Mount Duckabush and Mount Steel with snowfields, the valley dropping away in layered greens.

nodes.name: Lake Ben
nodes.description: A small, hidden tarn tucked in the basin south of O'Neil Pass, reached only by picking your own way down heather and rock.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: boulders and heather; midground: a small round dark-blue lake; sky: light blue; landmark: rocky shoulder of O'Neil Peak.

nodes.name: Marmot Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6 (separate 7-12 group site).
camp.notes: Compost toilet may be available. NPS: 18.9 mi from Staircase with about 6,850 ft gain. Camp in pre-existing sites; fragile meadows.

nodes.description: A small green lake sits in a saddle with a big flat rock above it, perfect for watching the evening light climb up Mount Duckabush and Mount Steel. Marmots whistle from the boulders.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a broad flat rock with a tent; midground: a round jade lake ringed by heather; sky: sunset dithered light red/yellow/light magenta; landmark: twin snowy peaks across the Duckabush valley.

nodes.name: Hart Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6; cross-country camp area booked by calling the WIC.
camp.notes: Rec.gov: compost toilet may be available; vegetation fragile, stay on trails.

nodes.description: Bigger and quieter than Marmot Lake, Hart Lake lies close under a dark ridge, with Mount Duckabush watching over its shoulder.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: heather bench; midground: a long blue lake under a steep dark-grey ridge; sky: light blue with puffy white; landmark: Mount Duckabush reflected in the water.

nodes.name: Lake LaCrosse

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Cross-country camp area (not self-bookable online; call the WIC).
camp.notes: About 1.4 mi and ~400 ft above Marmot Lake via a signed way trail. Elk herds commonly browse the slopes beyond.

nodes.description: The highest of the three lakes, cupped in rock and meadow with the whole basin spread below. On the steep slopes beyond, elk move slowly through the grass like brown clouds.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a meadow edge with avalanche lilies; midground: a deep-blue alpine lake with snow patches on the far shore; sky: bright blue dither; landmark: a herd of tiny elk on a green slope above the lake.

nodes.name: Upper Duckabush

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Sits at the junction of the Duckabush River, Home Sweet Home and O'Neil Pass trails. From the Duckabush trailhead the river must be forded just north of camp; it can be impassable in winter, early summer and after heavy rain. Rec.gov labels it 'Not Accessible from Staircase' (the North Fork Skokomish approach is closed in 2026).

nodes.description: Where the Duckabush is still a young river, camp tucks into the forest beside a gravel bar. Three trails meet here, and each one climbs toward a different kind of high country.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a three-way signpost; midground: a clear rushing river with a gravel bar; sky: grey-blue; landmark: steep forested slope rising toward hidden meadows.

nodes.name: LaCrosse Pass Trail junction (Duckabush)
nodes.description: A side trail turns north and immediately gets serious, switchbacking up the steep wall of the valley toward LaCrosse Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost and a pack leaning on it; midground: a steep forested slope; sky: small patch of blue; landmark: a bright gap in the canopy far above hinting at the pass.

nodes.name: LaCrosse Pass
nodes.description: A meadowy ridge-top between the Duckabush and the West Fork Dosewallips. There is no water up here, only wind, heather, and wide views both ways.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: low heather and rocks; midground: rounded meadow ridge; sky: wide blue with dithered horizon haze; landmark: Mount Anderson's massif to the north.

nodes.name: Ten Mile Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 10 mi from the Duckabush trailhead with about 3,340 ft of cumulative climbing. Stock camp adjacent. Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass to park at the USFS trailhead.

nodes.description: Deep in the Duckabush valley the trail levels beside the river, and old cedars make a roof over a quiet camp.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a camp stove steaming; midground: huge redcedar trunks; sky: dim grey-green; landmark: the river glinting cyan through trunks.

nodes.name: Olympic National Park boundary (Duckabush River Trail)
nodes.description: A small sign marks where The Brothers Wilderness of the national forest becomes the national park wilderness; from here a permit, a bear canister and patience are required.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a brown boundary sign on a post; midground: forest trail; sky: hidden; landmark: river sound represented by a glimpse of white water.

nodes.name: Fivemile Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest (The Brothers Wilderness) camp; no park permit needed here (verify USFS rules).
camp.notes: Popular camping and fishing area on the north side of Big Hump, about 650 ft below its crest; origin point of the 2011 Duckabush fire.

nodes.description: Down the far side of the big hill, the trail finds the river again at a sandy, popular camp where people fish and soak sore feet.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a fishing line over a pool; midground: river bend; sky: pale blue; landmark: silver snags from an old burn on the slope above.

nodes.name: Big Hump
nodes.description: A tight stack of switchbacks on dark, lichen-dotted rock lifts you over a forested knob through an old burn, with views down the bright river valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: switchback on dark rock with orange lichen dither; midground: silver dead snags; sky: blue; landmark: the Duckabush valley rolling away to the west.

nodes.name: Duckabush Trailhead
nodes.description: A gravel lot off a potholed forest road, a pit toilet, and a wide old roadbed heading into big-leaf maples. The river is already whispering somewhere to the left.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a dusty parking lot with a single car; midground: a trail sign reading DUCKABUSH; sky: pale blue; landmark: moss-draped bigleaf maples.

nodes.name: Home Sweet Home

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Compost toilet. Rec.gov: 13.5 mi from Staircase; currently 'not accessible via Staircase' because the North Fork Skokomish trail is closed below Home Sweet Home after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire. Reachable from the Duckabush/Upper Duckabush side.

nodes.description: A cupped meadow just below First Divide where the creek wanders in loops and deer pick through the flowers at dusk. The name tells you how it feels.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wildflower meadow with a deer; midground: a meandering silver stream; sky: soft evening dither, light magenta/blue; landmark: rocky ridges of Mount Steel above the meadow.

nodes.name: First Divide

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.water: None reliable at the divide itself; streams below on either side.
camp.notes: Listed as a (closed) wilderness campsite on the NPS Bear Gulch Fire page in 2026. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).

nodes.description: A low, forested gap where the trail crosses from the Skokomish side to the Duckabush side. Through the trees, the first real mountains of the trip appear all at once.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail crest with a small sign; midground: subalpine firs; sky: bright blue; landmark: Mount Steel and the upper Duckabush peaks framed in a gap.

nodes.name: Two Bear Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 11.6 mi from Staircase, about 2,780 ft of climbing. Trail brushy between Two Bear and First Divide.

nodes.description: A little bench in the steep upper forest, the last flat ground before the climb to the divide.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small tent on duff; midground: steep hemlock slope; sky: grey; landmark: a bear track pressed in mud near the stream.

nodes.name: Nine Stream Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 9.6 mi from Staircase, about 1,180 ft gain. Stock camp adjacent. The Nine Stream ford can be deep and swift in high snowmelt or heavy rain.

nodes.description: The valley narrows and the trail meets a cold side stream that must be waded when the snow is melting. Camp sits in big timber just beyond.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a hiker wading with poles; midground: a frothing stream; sky: grey; landmark: tall dark firs.

nodes.name: Camp Pleasant

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 6.7 mi from Staircase, about 712 ft gain. Stock camp adjacent.

nodes.description: True to its name: a flat, friendly camp near the river under old trees, an easy first night out of Staircase.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: picnic of a camp stove and two mugs; midground: grassy flat; sky: blue; landmark: river glimmer.

nodes.name: Six Ridge Trail junction (North Fork Skokomish)
nodes.description: The Six Ridge trail crosses the river and heads straight up a long, waterless ridge; five dry miles separate this junction from the spring at Belview.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost; midground: a footbridge over the river; sky: grey-blue; landmark: a steep forested ridge.

nodes.name: Big Log Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 5.3 mi from Staircase, about 570 ft gain. The Black and White Lakes primitive trail leaves the North Fork trail here.

nodes.description: A camp named for a fallen giant whose trunk is wider than you are tall. A steep side path starts here for the Black and White Lakes.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: an enormous fallen log covered in moss and small hemlocks; midground: camp clearing; sky: grey-green; landmark: river through trees.

nodes.name: Spike Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 3.5 mi from Staircase, about 630 ft gain. Sits just past the Flapjack Lakes trail junction.

nodes.description: Just past the Flapjack Lakes junction, a little camp with a pit toilet where the old roadbed walking ends and the real forest begins.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a wooden privy roof among ferns; midground: flat camp; sky: grey; landmark: fire-scarred snags on the slope (post-2025).

nodes.name: Flapjack Lakes Trail junction
nodes.description: A sign points uphill to the Flapjack Lakes, four miles and some 2,400 feet above.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost; midground: trail rising into forest; sky: hidden; landmark: a cascading creek.

nodes.name: Slide Camp (North Fork Skokomish)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 1.5 mi from the Staircase trailhead. Exact location not verified; placed by mileage.

nodes.description: A small riverside camp barely an hour from the car, handy for a late start.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent by river cobbles; midground: an old rockslide of mossy boulders; sky: grey; landmark: green river pool.

nodes.name: Staircase Rapids Loop junction (Rapids Bridge)
nodes.description: Here a suspension bridge swings across the North Fork above the Staircase Rapids, where the river spills down a stair-step of ledges in green and white.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: suspension bridge cables; midground: stepped rapids, white foam over green; sky: pale blue; landmark: towering Douglas-firs on both banks.

nodes.name: Staircase Trailhead (Staircase Ranger Station)
nodes.description: At the end of the road along Lake Cushman, a small ranger station sits under tall Douglas-firs beside the river. In 2026 the fire-scarred slopes above are a reminder that this forest is still healing.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rustic ranger station with a flagpole; midground: parking lot and trail sign; sky: blue with a faint haze; landmark: a ridge of blackened and silver snags above green forest.

nodes.name: Staircase Campground

camp.reservation_or_quota: Front-country campground (49 sites).
camp.water: Flush toilets and drinking water in summer season only.
camp.notes: Reopened July 8, 2026 with the Staircase developed area.

nodes.description: Forty-nine sites under big trees beside the North Fork, with the Rapids Loop a short stroll away.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: picnic table and lantern; midground: tents among firs; sky: night dither with stars; landmark: river sound as a white streak.

nodes.name: Smith Lake / Black and White Lakes trail junction (Flapjack Lakes Trail)
nodes.description: Half a mile below the Flapjack Lakes, a rougher trail branches toward Black and White Lakes and Smith Lake.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost; midground: steep trail with roots; sky: blue patches; landmark: a glimpse of jagged Sawtooth peaks.

nodes.name: Flapjack Lakes

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Quota area (includes Gladys Divide); reservation season June 15-Oct 15, 2026. Camp in designated sites only; max 6 per site, separate 7-12 group site. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Two vault toilets (do not urinate in them; they are flown out). Narrow isthmus between the lakes is not for camping. A seasonal backcountry ranger may camp on a wooden platform.

nodes.description: Two round lakes lie side by side like pancakes on a griddle, ringed by forest and watched over by the jagged Sawtooth Range. Evening light turns the peaks pink and the water silver.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a narrow isthmus between two round lakes; midground: dark firs on the shore; sky: alpenglow dithered light magenta/blue; landmark: jagged grey Sawtooth peaks with snow streaks.

nodes.name: Gladys Divide
nodes.description: A meadowed saddle between Mount Gladys and the rocky spire of Mount Cruiser, looking down into the Hamma Hamma country.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: heather and boulders; midground: a meadow saddle; sky: deep blue; landmark: the needle of Mount Cruiser.

nodes.name: Black and White Lakes

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.water: The lakes (treat). No water on the steep trail up from Big Log.
camp.notes: Small subalpine tarns at the junction of the Black and White Lakes primitive trail and the Smith Lake trail. Brushy, unmaintained; snow lingers late.

nodes.description: Two little tarns, one dark and one bright, perched on an open ridge with sweeping views back to the peaks above the North Fork.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a dark tarn and a pale tarn side by side; midground: heather ridge; sky: blue; landmark: Mount Skokomish and the North Fork peaks.

nodes.name: Smith Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.notes: Steep, rocky descent from Black and White Lakes.

nodes.description: A forest-rimmed lake below the ridge, reached by a steep, rocky drop from the Black and White Lakes.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rocky trail; midground: a green lake in a bowl of firs; sky: light blue; landmark: a cliff band above.

nodes.name: Wagonwheel Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. CLOSED in 2026: listed among wilderness campsites closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (NPS fire page updated 2026-09-18).
camp.water: Wagonwheel Lake and its outlet stream (treat).
camp.notes: Small lake with picnic spots high above it; no toilets.

nodes.description: A small lake under higher peaks at the top of one of the steepest trails in the park. You earn every foot of it.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a hiker bent over trekking poles; midground: a small dark lake below; sky: blue; landmark: Copper Mountain's ridges.

nodes.name: Success Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.notes: At the unbridged Success Creek ford, just above the Graves Creek crossing (WTA puts the crossing at 3.7 mi from the trailhead). Rec.gov text still mentions hanging food, but bear canisters are now required parkwide.

nodes.description: Graves Creek runs cool and shady in a deep gorge here, and an orange marker on a stump shows where to wade Success Creek.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: an orange-blazed stump; midground: a clear creek confluence; sky: dim green; landmark: steep gorge walls.

nodes.name: Wynoochee Pass Trail junction
nodes.description: Subalpine meadows begin where the Wynoochee Pass trail joins from the south.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost in meadow; midground: open meadow and small firs; sky: blue; landmark: Sundown Pass skyline.

nodes.name: Sundown Lake Trail / South Fork Skokomish Trail junction
nodes.description: In a meadowy hollow just below Sundown Pass, the trail from Graves Creek meets the South Fork Skokomish trail climbing from the south; the lake is a few minutes away.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost in heather; midground: meadow hollow with small firs; sky: late-afternoon gold dither; landmark: the notch of Sundown Pass above.

nodes.name: Sundown Pass
nodes.description: A gentle saddle on the park boundary where the South Fork Skokomish trail tops out. Snow can linger on the steep slopes around it.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: snow patch; midground: heather saddle; sky: sunset dither; landmark: Six Ridge stretching east.

nodes.name: Lake Sundown

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.notes: Subalpine lake at the west end of the Six Ridge route; NPS: 7.3 mi from Graves Creek trailhead, gross gain about 3,918 ft.

nodes.description: A small lake in a meadow basin that catches the last of the evening sun, as its name promises.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent at the lake edge; midground: still water reflecting orange sky; sky: sunset bands dithered light red/yellow/blue; landmark: Six Ridge silhouette.

nodes.name: McGravey Lakes

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Cross-country camp area (call WIC).
camp.notes: Route between Belview and McGravey Lakes is hard to follow in places.

nodes.description: Small ridge-top tarns among meadows and mountain hemlock, a rare drink of water on the long ridge.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small tarn; midground: meadow knolls; sky: blue; landmark: distant Olympus peaks to the north.

nodes.name: Belview Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.notes: Rec.gov: 6.4 mi from the North Fork Skokomish trail near Big Log, ~3,000 ft gain, with no water for the first 5 mi. In 2026 the Six Ridge trail east of Belview is closed (Bear Gulch Fire); Lake Sundown to Belview has reopened. Rec.gov lists it as 'not accessible via Staircase'.

nodes.description: A ridge-top camp with a spring and a long view, the 'beautiful view' its name hints at, across the North Fork Skokomish to the peaks.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a spring trickling into a small pool; midground: ridge meadow; sky: blue; landmark: Mount Skokomish and Mount Steel across the valley.

nodes.name: Mount Olson / Lake Success way trail junction
nodes.description: A faint way trail drops off the ridge toward Lake Success; meadows here are crisscrossed by game trails that fool the eye.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small cairn; midground: confusing braided paths through meadow; sky: grey fog dither; landmark: Mount Olson's shoulder.

nodes.name: Lake Success

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Cross-country camp area (call WIC).
camp.notes: Reached by a way trail from the Six Ridge trail near Mount Olson.

nodes.description: A hidden lake below Mount Olson, quiet as a held breath.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: lakeshore rocks; midground: small blue lake; sky: light blue; landmark: Mount Olson.

nodes.name: North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Fork Ranger Station)
nodes.description: At the end of a narrow gravel road, a small ranger station and a primitive campground sit beside a wide, rocky river. The trail starts behind a signpost and slips into wind-shaped rain forest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a signpost and a pack; midground: small cabin ranger station; sky: grey-blue dither; landmark: a broad river bar with distant snowy Mount Zindorf up-valley.

nodes.name: North Fork Campground (Quinault)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Primitive front-country campground (9 sites).
camp.notes: Open in 2026; narrow winding gravel road not recommended for RVs or trailers.

nodes.description: Nine primitive sites at the road's end, the quietest car camp in the valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tarp shelter over a table in rain; midground: alders; sky: rain streaks dithered grey; landmark: river.

nodes.name: Wolf Bar

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Five sites at the forest edge; Leave-No-Trace camping also possible on the gravel bar.

nodes.description: The last big flat beside the river, shaded by spruce over a carpet of sword fern, with a wide gravel bar for watching the sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: sword ferns; midground: huge Sitka spruce; sky: open over a pale gravel bar; landmark: braided river channels.

nodes.name: Wild Rose Creek ford
nodes.description: The trail dives into a side canyon where Wild Rose Creek must be crossed without a bridge: dry stepping stones in late summer, a raging chute in early summer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: steep muddy bank; midground: a rocky creek in a canyon with white water; sky: hidden; landmark: a yellow-jacket nest hanging in an alder (late summer).

nodes.name: Halfway House

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: NPS: 2 sites directly off the trail, 2.6 mi past Wolf Bar. Site of a long-gone lodge; WTA describes several sandy sites incl. one for a large group. Location approximate (NPS trail data spur near Wild Rose Creek).

nodes.description: Sandy campsites mark the spot where a lodge once stood; now there is only a gravel bar, an emerald river, and the high forested ridges of the Press Expedition's route.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: sandy tent pad; midground: emerald river under a gravel bar; sky: blue gap; landmark: forested ridges layered in greens.

nodes.name: Elip Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Four sites on the north side of Elip Creek; the privy is across the creek on the south side. Elip Creek must be forded. The Elip Creek (connector) trail to the Skyline starts right here.

nodes.description: Elip Creek must be waded to reach camp, and its privy oddly sits on the other bank. A steep connector climbs from here to the Skyline ridge.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wading hiker; midground: creek mouth into big river; sky: grey; landmark: old sign reading 'Skyline Trail 4.6'.

nodes.name: Trapper Shelter

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.water: Nearby creeks; a 2023 trip report found no good water at Trapper.
camp.notes: Shelter is for day and emergency use only; two small campsites behind it with a privy.

nodes.description: An old three-sided log shelter waits in the big trees, meant for storms and emergencies, with two small tent spots tucked behind.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rough-hewn log shelter with shake roof; midground: giant hemlocks; sky: rain dither; landmark: a smoke-darkened beam with carved initials.

nodes.name: Sixteen Mile Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Camp is on the far bank after the Sixteen Mile river ford (normally knee- to thigh-deep and swift in summer; hazardous or impassable in heavy rain or snowmelt). The name predates current mileage: the camp is about 12 mi from today's trailhead.

nodes.description: The trail runs straight into the North Fork, and the only way on is through it: cold, fast, and knee-deep on a good day. Camp waits in the forest on the far side.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: boots tied to a pack, bare feet on cobbles; midground: wide swift river with white braids; sky: grey-blue; landmark: steep flanks of Mount Lawson up-valley.

nodes.name: Skyline Primitive Trail junction (Low Divide)
nodes.description: Just before Low Divide, after one more unbridged creek, the Skyline trail ends its long ridge journey here.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: signpost; midground: forested meadow; sky: blue; landmark: Mount Seattle's slopes.

nodes.name: Low Divide

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee.
camp.notes: Three sites within sight of the periodically staffed Low Divide Ranger Cabin plus two more about 1/4 mi beyond. Rec.gov allows fires in existing rings even though the NPS also bans fires above 3,500 ft generally (verify). No camping near Lake Margaret or Lake Mary. Way trail to Martin's Park leaves from the south end of Lake Margaret. Fires (fact check 2026-10-08): set to no campfires. NPS's North Fork Quinault page puts Low Divide at 3,600-3,602 ft and says campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft; Recreation.gov's 'Low Divide' division text says campfires are permitted in existing rings. The park-wide 3,500-ft regulation is used here; confirm with the WIC. NPS: three sites within sight of the ranger cabin plus two more 1/4 mile beyond; no camping near Lake Margaret or Lake Mary.

nodes.description: Forested meadows, little lakes, and a ranger cabin sit on the low saddle between the Quinault and the Elwha, the same gap the Press Expedition struggled over in 1890. Mount Christie and Mount Seattle lean in close.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: meadow with avalanche lilies; midground: log ranger cabin; sky: light blue with dithered cloud; landmark: craggy Mount Christie with snowfields.

nodes.name: Lake Margaret
nodes.description: A small, still lake just past Low Divide where the Quinault trail becomes the Elwha trail. No camping here; just sit and watch the reflections.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: lily pads and sedges; midground: a small calm lake; sky: reflected peaks; landmark: Mount Seattle mirrored in water.

nodes.name: Irely Lake (Big Creek) Trailhead
nodes.description: A short walk down the North Fork road from the ranger station, a trail starts below a terrace of wind-thrown giants and heads for Irely Lake and the long climb to Three Lakes.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trailhead post; midground: tangle of fallen trees and young hemlock; sky: grey; landmark: huckleberry head-high.

nodes.name: Irely Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. (hidden Rec.gov division; call WIC).
camp.notes: Holds water in spring; more marsh than lake by late summer. Bridge over the creek fixed 10/2024.

nodes.description: A shallow lake that turns to marsh by late summer, ringed with old cedars and alive with birds and frogs.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: cedar puncheon boardwalk; midground: reedy lake with lily pads; sky: grey-blue; landmark: a great blue heron.

nodes.name: Big Creek ford
nodes.description: The trail plunges down a loose ravine to the canyon floor where a metal bridge used to be. Now you wade Big Creek, the last water for nearly three miles of switchbacks.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: steep muddy ravine; midground: a boulder-filled creek; sky: dim; landmark: a twisted remnant of old bridge on the bank.

nodes.name: Three Lakes

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.water: Outlet stream just north of camp; lakes (treat).
camp.notes: Plenty of sites; pit toilet with a view. Closed to stock camping. Frogs may croak all night. Near the trail stands what WTA calls the world's largest Alaska yellow-cedar (about 12 ft diameter).

nodes.description: Meadows of beargrass and little lakes half-filled with sphagnum moss open up after miles of silver fir and yellow-cedar. Frogs sing all night, and the stars come out enormous.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: beargrass plumes; midground: a mossy shallow lake; sky: night with dithered stars; landmark: a giant broken-topped yellow-cedar.

nodes.name: Reflection Lake
nodes.description: A small lake glimpsed below the trail to the east, holding the sky like a mirror.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: trail edge with huckleberry; midground: lake below; sky: mirrored blue; landmark: ridge of meadows and tarns.

nodes.name: Skyline Trail / Elip Creek Trail junction
nodes.description: On a steep, scrubby slope the Elip Creek trail tops out onto the Skyline route. Room for one poor tent; better camps lie north and south.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a signpost; midground: brushy slope; sky: moody grey cloud; landmark: the North Fork valley far below.

nodes.name: Three Prune Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.water: Small streams on either side of camp: the LAST reliable water for 5.2 mi until Kimta Peak basin.
camp.notes: Main site beside an old gnarled tree in a meadow.

nodes.description: A gnarled old tree stands alone in a meadow, sheltering a few tent spots. Fill every bottle here: the ridge ahead is dry.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: water bottles lined up by a stream; midground: a twisted solitary tree; sky: blue; landmark: first glimpse of Mount Olympus far to the north.

nodes.name: Kimta Peak basin

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Cross-country camp ('Kimta Peak', no campfires; call WIC).
camp.water: Small seasonal creek in the basin.
camp.notes: First water after Three Prune.

nodes.description: A high basin below Kimta Peak with a seasonal trickle of water and long views west over the Queets.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a trickle over rocks; midground: rocky basin; sky: wide blue; landmark: the Queets valley in blue haze.

nodes.name: Lake Beauty Pass (Lake Beauty trail junction)
nodes.description: After cairned rock gardens, Hee Haw Pass and long scree traverses, the trail reaches the side path down to Lake Beauty.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a cairn; midground: scree and meadow; sky: blue; landmark: south flank of Mount Olympus.

nodes.name: Lake Beauty

camp.reservation_or_quota: Wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov permit 4098362), $8/adult/night + $6 reservation fee. Group size max 6.
camp.notes: 0.3 mi side trail, about 400 ft below the Skyline.

nodes.description: A perfect subalpine bowl with Mount Olympus filling the sky across the valley. People who come here tend to stay an extra day.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wildflowers at lakeshore; midground: a clear blue lake in a bowl; sky: blue; landmark: glaciated Mount Olympus, white and huge.

nodes.name: Seattle Creek crossing
nodes.description: The trail drops a thousand feet through ravines to cross Seattle Creek, then claws back up switchbacks under Mount Noyes and Mount Seattle.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rocky gully; midground: a cascading creek; sky: narrow; landmark: craggy south face of Mount Noyes.

nodes.name: Quinault Rain Forest Ranger Station
nodes.description: A small ranger station on the North Shore Road where the Kestner Homestead and Maple Glade loops begin. In 2026 the station and its wilderness desk are closed.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: interpretive sign; midground: ranger station building and footbridge; sky: grey drizzle dither; landmark: moss-dripping bigleaf maples.

nodes.name: Kestner Homestead
nodes.description: An old barn, a farmhouse and rusting tools stand in a field the rain forest is slowly reclaiming, left by families who homesteaded the valley from 1889.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rusted farm machinery in grass; midground: weathered grey barn and house; sky: soft grey; landmark: elk grazing at the field edge.

nodes.name: Quinault Rain Forest Nature Trail trailhead (Olympic National Forest)
nodes.description: On the lake's south shore, a national forest parking lot opens onto boardwalks through spruce and hemlock dripping with moss.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: wooden boardwalk; midground: giant Sitka spruce; sky: green-grey; landmark: interpretive sign shaped like a leaf.

nodes.name: Cascade Falls
nodes.description: A creek slides down mossy rock steps in thin white ribbons, the halfway treat on the Quinault Loop.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: footbridge; midground: tiered falls over mossy rock; sky: none; landmark: maidenhair ferns.

nodes.name: Lake Quinault lodge area (in-game business name: The Mossback Lodge)
nodes.description: A grand old shingled lodge looks out over the lake from a lawn of sun and rain. In-game this privately run lodge appears under the fictional name The Mossback Lodge.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: lawn with Adirondack chairs; midground: big shingled lodge with many windows; sky: sunset over the lake dithered light red/blue; landmark: the long grey lake and forested hills.

segments.notes: Crosses Graves Creek on a high bridge; junction is about 200 ft past it (WTA). Mileage approximate.
Follows an old road grade, climbing about 500 ft to a low saddle, then drops steeply to Pony Bridge over a narrow gorge (NPS: ~2.5 mi trailhead to Pony Bridge).

Climbs above a scenic gorge then back to river level; Fire Creek is crossed on a foot-log 3/4 mi past Pony Bridge (NPS). Rec.gov calls Fire Creek '4 miles from trailhead' (conflict). Foot-logs can be slick or damaged after storms.
Rolling up-and-down riverside forest; watch for elk and bears between the trees. NPS gives 4.4 mi Pony Bridge to O'Neil Creek. Side trail descends ~100 ft to camp.
Small climbs and descents; No Name Creek (WTA ~8 mi) and Pyrites Creek are crossed on footlog bridges.

Gradual continuous climb. About 1/2 mi before the chalet there is a gate (close it behind you), then the high bridge. Split of NPS's 3.2 mi Pyrites-to-Enchanted Valley figure is estimated from WTA's description.

segments.snow_free_typical: Bridge can hold snow into spring; trail otherwise low-elevation
segments.notes: High bridge about 20 ft above the river may be snow-covered in spring. 2026: a washed-out section about 1/3 mi before the chalet/campsites forces a river ford or steep route-finding up a hillside (NPS trail conditions 9/29/26).
Chalet sits in the meadow by the camps; closed to the public. Distance approximate; level.

segments.snow_free_typical: Snow-covered above 3,500 ft Nov-June; lower part usually clear by June
segments.notes: Steady climb out of the valley. NPS calls the White Creek crossing 'Mile 16'. Romano (via Mountaineers) gives 3.2 mi chalet to O'Neil Pass Trail junction; split from NPS GIS geometry.

segments.snow_free_typical: above 3,500 ft snow-covered Nov-June; typically snow-free mid-Jul to mid-Oct
segments.notes: White Creek must be forded (no bridge); swift and deep in heavy rain or snowmelt, typically fall through early summer, and may be unfordable (NPS 9/29/26).

segments.snow_free_typical: above 3,500 ft snow-covered Nov-June; typically snow-free mid-Jul to mid-Oct
segments.notes: Crosses a rocky creek draining White Mountain, then switchbacks across open slopes to the final steep climb to the 4,464-ft pass. Steep, rocky and narrow at times. NPS: Enchanted Valley to Anderson Pass ~5.2 mi with ~2,500 ft gain; trailhead to pass 18.2 mi. Romano (via Mountaineers) gives 1.9 mi from the O'Neil junction to the Anderson Glacier spur at the pass; NPS GIS geometry suggests ~1.5 mi.

segments.snow_free_typical: Late July through mid-October (NPS best season)
segments.notes: Low-maintenance trail contouring high above the East Fork through montane forest and subalpine meadow; NPS lists 1,940 ft gain. Small tent sites in White Creek Basin partway along (cross-country camp, call WIC; one 2022 trip report calls it 'a short mile' above the junction). Closed to stock. Various small streams for water. No bear wires; canisters required.
No trail. Lake Ben lies about 0.9 mi straight-line south of O'Neil Pass (GNIS positions), roughly 500-700 ft below; cross-country heather and rock. Mileage unknown.
Descends from the pass to Marmot Lake in its saddle (WTA: 'just 1.2 miles'; 2015 trip report agrees).

About 0.6 mi of short steep way trail north to a signed junction (left Hart Lake, right LaCrosse), then about 0.5 mi to Hart Lake (2015 trip report; WTA says the junction is about 1 mi). Gain/loss estimated from DEM along a straight line.

Via the signed junction; Lake LaCrosse is about 400 ft higher and 1.4 mi beyond Marmot Lake (WTA; Romano: 0.6 + 0.8 mi). Elk often browse the slopes beyond. Gain/loss estimated from DEM along a straight line.
Back to the signed junction (~0.5 mi) then up to Lake LaCrosse (~0.8 mi). NPS warns the 'Hart Lake cutoff' and 'LaCrosse Lake cutoff' routes shown on some GPS maps are cross-country, not trails.

segments.snow_free_typical: Upper part snow-covered into July; lower part early July-October
segments.notes: O'Neil Pass Trail descends ~1,700 ft from Marmot Lake to the Duckabush. Mileage derived from NPS figures (Staircase-Marmot Lake 18.9 mi minus Staircase-Upper Duckabush 15.3 mi); NPS GIS gives ~3.3 mi.

segments.snow_free_typical: Early July-October (can be snow-free lower down much of the year)
segments.notes: The Upper Duckabush ford just north of the camp can be hazardous or impassable in winter, early summer, and during heavy rain or early-season melt (NPS 9/30/26). WTA says the LaCrosse Pass junction is about 1 mi from the trail's end; NPS GIS ~1.6 mi.

segments.snow_free_typical: Below 2,000 ft can be snow-free year-round
segments.notes: Lower-maintenance river trail; brushy and overgrown in places; at last report more than 50 trees down between the trailhead and the Upper Duckabush ford (NPS 9/30/26). Mileage derived: Upper Duckabush 17.5 mi from trailhead (Rec.gov) minus Ten Mile 10 mi minus 1.7.
NPS places the park boundary 6.2 mi from the trailhead (USFS page says 6.7 mi).
Olympic National Forest (The Brothers Wilderness). Fivemile Camp is about 5 mi from the trailhead (WTA: 10.6 mi round trip).
Climb ~650 ft back over Big Hump through the 2011 Duckabush burn; dead standing trees and unstable ground (USFS). Mileage estimated from NPS GIS geometry.

Easy grade for the first ~2.4 mi along an old roadbed and riverside forest, then tight switchbacks on loose rock up Big Hump (USFS); 'Snack Rock' viewpoint partway. A blue bag is advised for human waste around 4.2 mi where the terrain is rocky (WTA). Mileage estimated from NPS GIS geometry.

Steepest side of the LaCrosse Pass Trail. NPS: whole trail 6.4 mi between the West Fork Dosewallips and Duckabush junctions, 3,600-5,566 ft; split estimated from NPS GIS geometry. No water near the pass; no established campsites (camp on bare ground 200 ft from water). Several trees down (NPS 6/5/26).

West Fork Dosewallips side of the LaCrosse Pass Trail, from the pass down to the LaCrosse Pass Junction camp on the West Fork trail (northeast_dose node lacrosse_pass_junction, 0.5 mi above Honeymoon Meadows). Values mirror the identical northeast_dose segment lacrosse_pass_junction->lacrosse_pass (3.1 mi of the NPS 6.4 mi trail total); keep one copy when merging. Fact check 2026-10-08: this segment previously ended at honeymoon_meadows, which skipped the 0.5 mi between the junction and the camp.

segments.snow_free_typical: Snow and route-finding possible fall through early summer; typically clear mid-July to early October
segments.notes: Home Sweet Home Trail climbs ~1,500 ft from the Duckabush. NPS: First Divide to Duckabush junction 2.6 mi (4,688 to 2,695 ft); Home Sweet Home is ~0.8 mi below First Divide (Rec.gov 13.5 vs 12.7 mi). CLOSED in 2026 per NPS trail-conditions summary (Bear Gulch Fire), although the fire page lists the North Fork closure as ending at Home Sweet Home; verify.
Short climb out of the meadow to the 4,688-ft divide. WTA says about 1 mi. CLOSED in 2026 (Home Sweet Home Trail, NPS conditions 9/30/26).

Brushy between Two Bear and First Divide. CLOSED 2026 (Bear Gulch Fire); burn-scar hazards: falling snags, rockfall, landslides. Mileage from Rec.gov (Two Bear 11.6) and NPS (First Divide 12.7; NPS conditions page says 12.5).

segments.snow_free_typical: Low elevations year-round; snow possible Nov-May
segments.notes: Descends steeply through forest. CLOSED 2026.
Nine Stream ford at camp can be deep and swift in snowmelt or heavy rain (NPS). CLOSED 2026.
Mileage derived from Rec.gov (Camp Pleasant 6.7) and GIS (junction ~0.3 mi past Big Log at 5.3). CLOSED 2026.
CLOSED 2026.
Rec.gov: Big Log 5.3 mi, Spike Camp 3.5 mi from the trailhead. CLOSED 2026.
Spike Camp sits just past the Flapjack junction (GIS). NPS: junction is 3.5 mi from Staircase (Flapjack Lakes 7.5 mi total, 4.0 mi from junction); WTA says 3.7 mi. CLOSED 2026.
Gentle decommissioned roadbed. Slide Camp position by Rec.gov mileage only (1.5 mi). CLOSED 2026.
CLOSED 2026 beyond the Rapids Loop junction.
OPEN 2026: part of the Staircase Rapids Loop (2.1 mi loop; reopened July 8, 2026). Suspension bridge over the river at the rapids.
Climbs along Madeline Creek (mini waterfalls) past Madeline Creek and Donahue Creek camps (hidden/closed Rec.gov divisions). CLOSED 2026. Closed to stock. Split of NPS 4.0 mi figure from GIS.

segments.snow_free_typical: Late June through September (NPS best season)
segments.notes: Final steep pitch to the lakes. CLOSED 2026.
Gladys Divide Primitive Trail, 3,900 to 5,050 ft. Closed to stock. CLOSED 2026.

Brushy and narrow with several streams needing rock-hopping or wet feet. NPS: 2.2 mi from the Flapjack trail through Black and White Lakes to Smith Lake (3,500-4,400-3,950 ft); split from GIS. CLOSED 2026.
Black and White Lakes Primitive Trail: 2.5 mi, 1,500 to 4,400 ft, steep, brushy, unmaintained, NO water sources. Closed to stock. CLOSED 2026.
Steep and rocky descent to Smith Lake. CLOSED 2026.
About 3,200 ft of gain in under 3 mi; limited water; faint in places and very hard to follow in snow; brushy traverse before the lake. Closed to stock. CLOSED 2026 (Bear Gulch Fire).

Steep climb with NO water for about 5 mi (until Belview); Seven Stream is the last water near the bottom. CLOSED 2026 from the Mount Olson way-trail junction (east edge of Belview) down to the North Fork. Split of Rec.gov's 6.4 mi (North Fork to Belview) from GIS.
Meadows between Six Ridge Pass and the Lake Success/Mount Olson junction are hard to follow with confusing game and way trails; GPS and a communication device recommended (NPS).
Way trail; mileage not published. Lake Success is about 1.1 mi straight-line north-northwest of the junction (GNIS). CLOSED 2026? (junction is the eastern limit of the reopened section; verify).

Repeated gains and losses with route-finding challenges; sections between Belview and McGravey Lakes are hard to follow (NPS). Split of the NPS 4.2 mi (10.6 total minus 6.4) from GIS. Reopened 2026 (Lake Sundown to Belview).

segments.snow_free_typical: Mid-July through October; ice axe recommended near Lake Sundown/Sundown Pass when snowy
segments.notes: Crosses Six Ridge Pass (high point of the route, ~4,650 ft per NPS). Steep, exposed slopes near Lake Sundown/Sundown Pass. Reopened 2026.
Short drop from the lake to the junction with the South Fork Skokomish Trail below Sundown Pass.

segments.snow_free_typical: Mid-July through October; ice axe recommended when snowy
segments.notes: Side climb on the South Fork Skokomish Trail to the 4,100-ft saddle on the park boundary (USFS trail continues south to the South Fork Skokomish trailhead). Mileage measured from NPS GIS geometry; not published.

Mileage derived (NPS 7.3 mi trailhead to Lake Sundown minus WTA 6.2 mi to the Wynoochee junction, minus 0.3). STATUS (fact check 2026-10-08): treated as CLOSED. The NPS trail conditions row 'Six Ridge Primitive Route, Graves Creek Trailhead to Lake Sundown, 7.3 mi' (updated 9/29/26) says 'Trail closed as of 8/1/25 due to Bear Gulch Fire'. hazards.name: White Creek ford below the O'Neil Pass junction
